seasonUncovered: At this position in Earth's orbit with a hypothetical 0° axial tilt, Earth's axis stands perpendicular to the Sun's rays, causing both hemispheres to receive sunlight at identical angles throughout the year. This uniform solar distribution results in equal day and night lengths across the Northern and Southern Hemispheres, with minimal temperature variations between them. Consequently, no seasonal variation occurs in either hemisphere—Earth would experience perpetual equinox-like conditions, eliminating the cyclic pattern of seasons that defines our current climate system.
